clue.text: Mother admitting son is controlling

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the first word takes the next inside itself

parts.note: Latin for mother, the old public-school word
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A domineering mother keeps her boy under her thumb.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it describes the principal device that governs others, as in a master switch.

clue.text: Continue when principal trace of contamination's finally removed

indicators.note: the final letter is taken away, the end being removed

parts.note: main means chief or principal
a taint is a trace of contamination

explanation.surface: Carry on once the last bit of pollution has been cleaned up.
explanation.definitionFit: To maintain something is to keep it going, so to continue it.

clue.text: Asking earnestly to take over from boxing instructor at the outset

indicators.note: boxing means putting in a box, so one part encloses the other

parts.note: to supplant is to displace and take someone's place

indicators.note: at the outset means at the start, so only the first letter is used

parts.note: the opening letter of instructor

explanation.surface: Replacing a boxing coach from the very start of training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing instructor' looks like a trainer in the ring; boxing is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A suppliant humbly begs or pleads, so as an adjective it means asking earnestly.

clue.text: Deserve to be informed after commencement

indicators.note: only what follows the beginning is kept, so the opening letter is lost

parts.note: to learn something is to be informed of it

explanation.surface: A graduate merits being told the news after the ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commencement' hints at an American graduation ceremony, but it just means the start of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn something is to merit it through one's efforts, to deserve it.

clue.text: That may be seen as almost suitable by mother

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: apt means fitting or suitable
a mother is a parent

explanation.surface: Someone judges a choice nearly right, as long as a mother approves.
explanation.definitionFit: Something apparent is visible or evident, which is what may be seen.

clue.text: Record defeat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to write something down for the record
second meaning: to crush or suppress, as in putting down a rebellion

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a sports result being logged; the two words are separate meanings of one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to note in writing and to suppress or quell by force.

clue.text: Combine to form new team after Alma's replaced by Georgia

indicators.note: replaced here means put back in a different arrangement, so the name's letters move

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: forming something new means making a fresh arrangement of the letters

parts.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A team is reshuffled when a player called Alma is swapped for one called Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Replaced by Georgia' looks like a substitution, but Alma is simply rearranged and GA follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To amalgamate is to merge separate things into one whole, to combine them.

clue.text: Muse for a time after hesitation over love

indicators.note: after puts the hesitation sound first and the article with the time second

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitating
taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone muses on romance after a pause.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'over' means the earlier letters sit above O.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Greek Muses, the patron of lyric and love poetry.

clue.text: Attempt to cover tip with it

indicators.note: covering something means wrapping around it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a try is an attempt
the tip of something is its end

explanation.surface: Someone tries to hide a gratuity along with something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tip' tempts as a waiter's gratuity; it is an end. 'With it' is the definition, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be with it is to be fashionable and up to date, which is to be trendy.

clue.text: Is unable to get tolerable port in China

parts.note: can't, cannot
on as in acceptable, as in 'that's not on'

explanation.surface: Someone cannot find decent port wine while in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the wine; it is a harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Canton is the older Western name for Guangzhou, a major southern Chinese harbour city.

clue.text: Fellow stashing wine on board — it's of great concern

indicators.note: to stash is to hide away, so the fellow keeps the drink tucked inside him

parts.note: taken as written; it splits to wrap the rest

indicators.note: being on board means being inside a vessel, so the whole lot sits within the next word

parts.note: a fellow is a man
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Someone smuggling drink aboard a ship is a serious worry.
explanation.walkthrough: Two containers nest: the wine sits inside the fellow, and that pair sits inside 'it', which splits around them. The 's is just 'is' leading to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something important matters a great deal, so it is a matter of serious concern.

clue.text: Humble when introduced to Lincoln

indicators.note: being introduced to something means being put into it

parts.note: Abe is the familiar name of President Abraham Lincoln
as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'

explanation.surface: A modest person meeting the great President Lincoln.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Humble' looks like an adjective describing someone; here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Humble used as a verb means to lower someone in dignity, the same sense as abase.

clue.text: Lie in shadow say

indicators.note: say signals we want the word as it is pronounced rather than as written

parts.note: to shadow someone is to tail them, follow them secretly

explanation.surface: Someone lies low, hiding in the shade.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale is a fabricated story, so telling one is a falsehood, a lie.

clue.text: Keep steadfast and carry on

parts.note: strong as in firm and resolute
to hold is to continue or persist, as in the weather holding

explanation.surface: It echoes the wartime motto Keep Calm and Carry On.
explanation.definitionFit: A keep is the fortified central tower of a castle, its last line of defence.

clue.text: Lax padres sadly found in many places

parts.note: wide as in loose, not tight or precise

indicators.note: sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are in disarray

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Careless priests are unfortunately seen everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Something widespread is distributed over a large area, so it is found in many places.

clue.text: Language barrier eventually overcome by one Scotsman then another

indicators.note: being overcome by something means being swallowed up within it

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

indicators.note: eventually means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the end letter of barrier
a second Scotsman, again Ian

explanation.surface: Two Scots find a way past a language barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside the first IAN to make IRAN, then the second IAN follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Iranian is the name given to the main tongue of Iran, also called Persian or Farsi.

clue.text: Count powerless to act against the Queen

parts.note: numb as in paralysed, unable to respond
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the royal cipher

explanation.surface: An aristocrat helpless to move against the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a nobleman to go with the Queen; it is the noun for a total.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is a tally, the total arrived at by counting, which is a number.

clue.text: Immunity for English politician after former partner gets into trouble

indicators.note: after sends the country and politician second, behind the former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: being in trouble means being in a mess, so the small word gets jumbled

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English
an MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: An English MP seeks legal protection after their ex lands in a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets into trouble' reads as one phrase, but 'into' is the letters to rearrange and 'trouble' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemption frees someone from an obligation or liability, which is an immunity.

clue.text: Drab grey colour worn by Thessaly's earliest sailors

indicators.note: something worn by another is carried around inside its covering

parts.note: slate is a bluish grey

indicators.note: earliest means first, so only the opening letter of the place name is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of Thessaly
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Dull grey uniforms are worn by Greek seamen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drab grey colour' reads as one phrase; drab is the noun, an old word for a slovenly woman. T goes between SLAT and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A drab and a slattern are both old words for a slovenly, untidy woman.

clue.text: Witness acts oddly before trial

indicators.note: oddly points to the odd-numbered positions, first and third

parts.note: first and third letters of acts
a trial is a test

explanation.surface: A witness behaves strangely ahead of a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trial' suggests a courtroom alongside 'witness', but it is just a test.
explanation.definitionFit: To witness a document is to sign confirming it, which is to attest or certify it.

clue.text: Anguish of French priest caught out after a wrongful act

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

indicators.note: out means removed, so that letter is taken away from the cleric

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: The distress of a French priest exposed after doing something wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' is the cricket abbreviation C, and 'out' removes it from the priest. A tort is a civil wrong in English law.
explanation.definitionFit: Torture is extreme suffering of mind or body, which is anguish.

clue.text: It occupies stylish poet

indicators.note: to occupy is to take up space inside, so the first word lives within the next

parts.note: swell as in smart and fashionable
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something takes over a fashionable writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Sitwell was an English poet of the twentieth century, as were her brothers Osbert and Sacheverell.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith Sitwell was a famous modernist English writer of verse, hence a poet.

clue.text: Contemplate drinking last of Oyster Stout

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so one word swallows the other

parts.note: to study is to consider carefully

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the following word

parts.note: the final letter of Oyster

explanation.surface: Musing over a pint of oyster stout, a real beer style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oyster Stout' looks like a beer; Stout is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stout as an adjective means strongly built and solid, which is sturdy.

clue.text: Volunteers holding up box found in Ancient Greek location

parts.note: to spar is to box
the TA, Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Volunteers carry a crate discovered at an archaeological site.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, the piece holding another up sits beneath it, so the volunteers come last.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparta was a powerful city-state of ancient Greece.

clue.text: Andre ultimately overwhelmed by poor Spurs failing to become successful

indicators.note: to be overwhelmed by something is to be engulfed inside it
a failing side falls apart, so the letters collapse into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the last letter of the name counts

parts.note: the final letter of Andre

explanation.surface: Tottenham Hotspur, nicknamed Spurs, are struggling despite a player called Andre.
explanation.walkthrough: Spurs is the nickname of Tottenham Hotspur, a London football club. The E joins the letters of poor Spurs before they are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperous means thriving and well off, which is to be successful.

clue.text: Cat edges away from ball

indicators.note: the edges are taken away, so the outer letters are dropped

parts.note: in cricket a bouncer is a short ball that rears up at the batsman

explanation.surface: A cat sidles away from a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Edges away' reads as the cat creeping off; it means the end letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: An ounce is the snow leopard, a wild cat of Central Asia.

clue.text: Quarrel with old man in street

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the following one

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A row breaks out with Dad out in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a brief petty argument, a minor quarrel.

clue.text: Part of answer found after time's up

indicators.note: in a down answer up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Part of a solution emerges once the time limit is over.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or section of something, which is a part of it.

clue.text: Row with Naomi initially carried by Vogue

indicators.note: something carried by another is held within it

parts.note: a rage is a craze or fashion, all the vogue

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the first letter is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of Naomi

explanation.surface: A quarrel involving supermodel Naomi Campbell, featured in Vogue magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a fight to match the celebrity gossip, but it means a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A range is a line or series, as in a mountain range, which is a row of peaks.

clue.text: Adjusted undies to hide the German's bottom

indicators.note: to hide something is to conceal it inside, so the garment wraps the next part
adjusted means altered or rearranged, so the letters change their order

parts.note: taken as written
der is the masculine German for the

explanation.definitionFit: The underside of anything is its lowest surface, which is its bottom.

clue.text: Live right by river running through the centre of Japanese city

indicators.note: something running through another passes inside it
the centre of a word is its middle, so the two central letters are kept

parts.note: the fourth and fifth of the eight letters
to be is to exist or live
R is the abbreviation for right
the Dee is a river in Scotland and Wales

explanation.surface: It reads as if describing a riverside life in a city in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japanese city' is the trap: the city is the Scottish one, and Japanese only supplies its middle letters, which wrap around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a major Scottish port, a city on the North Sea coast.

clue.text: Learn about girl finding a weapon

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word surrounds the next

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a girl's name
